articles.body: Disclosure: I work on PersonaXpand, a social media tool made by Nextoria in Dubai. This post is about how we built its MCP connector, which lets Claude and ChatGPT post, schedule and answer comments on a person's own accounts. The code patterns apply to any remote MCP server. Most MCP tutorials stop at a local server that talks over stdio. That works for a developer's own laptop. It stops working the moment you want a normal person to click "Connect" inside Claude or ChatGPT and have it just work. Then you need a remote server, and a remote server needs real OAuth . We built ours inside an existing ASP.NET Core 10 app with the official C# SDK ( ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore ). Here is what we learned, including three things that cost us days. 1. articles.title: Build a RAG Chatbot with LangChain and Chroma
articles.excerpt: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG, is a pattern that lets a language model answer questions from your own documents instead of only from its training data. We turn our documents into searchable v…
articles.body: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, or RAG, is a pattern that lets a language model answer questions from your own documents instead of only from its training data. We turn our documents into searchable vectors, then hand the most relevant passages to the model with each question. In this tutorial we build one with LangChain and Chroma, using free models that run locally. Key takeaways RAG grounds a language model in our own documents, so answers come from facts we control instead of from training memory. Chroma stores each chunk of text next to its embedding vector, and a similarity search finds the chunks that match a question. All-MiniLM-L6-v2 turns sentences into 384 number vectors, and it runs on a normal laptop CPU with no API key, according to its Hugging Face model card.
articles.author: Muhammad Saud

articles.title: Stop your voice agent interrupting itself on phone calls (Soniox STT v6 agent text, paced from the phone leg)
articles.excerpt: There's a bug every voice agent team hits eventually. The agent asks a question, gets three words in, stops, and says "Sorry, go ahead." Nobody said anything. The agent heard itself. In a browser demo…
articles.body: There's a bug every voice agent team hits eventually. The agent asks a question, gets three words in, stops, and says "Sorry, go ahead." Nobody said anything. The agent heard itself. In a browser demo you rarely see it. The browser's echo canceller is decent, you're wearing headphones, and the network is clean. On a real phone call it shows up a lot more, and it's one of the reasons an agent that felt great in testing starts "randomly" cutting itself off once it has a real number. Two launches in early November 2026 went right at this layer, so it's worth walking through what's actually happening. What shipped Soniox STT v6 (Nov 3). The headline feature is that the speech model now knows what your agent is saying.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
articles.excerpt: Researcher finds 35,000 Grok Build apps wide open to anyone who looked for them.
articles.body: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI, is leaking data—some of it proprietary business information and other sensitive secrets—from thousands of its users, including the very same Elon Musk-owned company that offers the platform, new research shows. The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. Except in rare cases, clicking those links opens the app and reveals all data associated with it.

articles.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.
articles.body: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world.
